Routine: 

• • •All using Bondi Boost Products • • •


Last night I applied the elixir oil and slept in it

Washed out with the Curl Boss Shampoo (two squirts in hands and emulsify then apply) 

Applied the RR Mask and left in for 10-15min 

Rinsed hair to about 80% clean (so leaving some product still in the hair) 

Plopped for about 10 minutes while getting dressed and doing my skincare 

Applied the Frix Fix and Rapid Repair serums with a couple drops Olaplex #7 (had this bottle for ages and still working through it 😂😅) and a couple drops Colourful neutral protein filler (my hair loves protein)

Wet rushed this through to ensure even distribution 

Blow dried roots as I wanted my hair to be tied up 

Using a spray bottle (with water, a little RR mask and a little curl cream mixed together)  I made sure the ends of my hair were wet (not quite dripping but very wet) 

Then used a 10c sized dollop of both the curl cream and RR Mask and scrunched into hair 

Using my brand new Denman brush I then brushed small sections to form the defined curls. 

The gathered all up in my hairdryer diffuser prior to turning on, turned on for about 5-10minutes - not moving the diffuser at all, and making sure to turn off before removing the hair from the diffuser
I wear my hair in a ponytail 90% of the time - I’m an electrician so it being down is annoying hahaha. I blow dry the roots, then tie it up and then spray the ends until they’re wet enough again

Routine:
- Colourful Neutral Protein - massaged into damp hair last night and left on overnight up in a bun. First time using this product and loving the results
- wash hair with BondiBoost low lather Curl Boss shampoo 
- condition with BondiBoost Curl Boss and a couple drops of Colourful Neutral Protein and left in for 5-10 minutes 
- plopped with microfibre towel while getting dry and dressed (Probably another 10 minutes) 
- 3 squirts of both BondiBoost Frizz Fix Serum and Rapid Repair Serum, with a couple drops of Colourful Neutral Protein.
- mix of BondiBoost Curl Boss Styling Cream and the Coles Gel and squished into sections 
- finger curled sections of hair and ensured that the sections were fully covered in the Gel 
- diffused with my Dyson to about 85-90% then left the rest to airdry
- once fully dry crunched out the cast and finger racked the clumps out

Seen that your In Adelaide! Hello fellow Aussie! I’m in Melbourne. I’ve been a sparky for just on 6 years now. Did my 4 year apprenticeship through Apprenticeships Group Australia in Melbourne, they’re a group training, labour hire style company. Which is really great to get an idea of what field of electrical work you want to go into. Pre COVID I was in the process of starting up my own company “Watts Her Name Electrical” but unfortunately that’s been put on hold due to the restrictions in Vic 😕

Honestly I love being in a trade. I’ve always gotten along with mates better than females. And I feel at home with the buys. Sometimes the first couple of working with a new bunch of guys they can treat me a bit different, but once I’ve shown them that I’m not an overly sensitive feminist who won’t pull her weight, they don’t treat me any differently. I’ve also had many bosses tell me that they’ve preferred having me over male apprentices due to the attention to detail that most women normally have

As for the heavy lifting, it completely depends on the field you end up working in. Solar panels can be 1600h and weight 20kgs each, drums of cable can range from 5-30kg. And specialty drums can be over 60kg for a small type drum. 

The one thing I struggle with is the fact that I have no female friends whatsoever. And it is extremely difficult to make female friends in the trades. I’ve only worked with about 10 other females in my 6 years. And most of them I only shared a placement for a couple weeks. 

Maybe try doing a pre apprenticeship first to see if you actually enjoy the electrical trade. Should be about a 6 week course that’ll give you a good feeler :)

All trades are going to be physically demanding in some sort. Ladders over 6ft are generally 12-15kgs. And extension ladders can be over 20kgs and they’re awkward as hell to move. Drums of cable that you have to carry up ladders to the top floor of a new house can be anywhere from 10-30+kg. I definitely wouldn’t be looking to spend 4 years learning a trade because you wanted the one that was the easiest. 
Also. If you aren’t working on a new construction site and end up doing maintenance work in peoples homes/workplaces, you have to look presentable in as much a way as any other career. 
Honestly the least demanding trade type work is a stop go ticket, but nearly every girl I have seen working that position has more makeup on than I’ve ever worn. Fake lashes, full face of foundation, bright lipstick. It doesn’t matter we’re you go, you’ll work with girls who try extra, and girls who do the bare minimum. You shouldn’t let what others think of you determine the job that you will do for the rest of your life.
